content:
Parity by 2030 is plausible but not certain.

1. A techno-economic model puts the **base-case parity year** between 2028 and 2031 [1].
2. In 2025 sodium-ion cells still cost more: 87 USD/kWh against 74 USD/kWh for LFP [2].
3. Scale is the swing factor: announced capacity totals 162 GWh per year by 2030, but only 31 GWh is under construction [3].

The main counter-view: *below 15,000 USD per tonne of lithium carbonate, LFP keeps its cost lead through 2030* [4].

citations.source_title: Techno-economic assessment of sodium-ion versus LFP cells for stationary storage
citations.quote: In the base case, sodium-ion cells reach cost parity with LFP between 2028 and 2031.
Average sodium-ion cell prices reached 87 USD/kWh in 2025, against 74 USD/kWh for LFP.
